body:
> **⚠️ Body repaired post-merge (2026-08-27).** Between this PR opening and merging, an
> implementer working a *different* lane ran `gh pr edit` against **3226** instead of
> **3227** and overwrote this body with #3222's — including a stray `Fixes #3222` trailer,
> which falsely auto-closed #3222 on merge. #3222 has been **reopened**; its real work is
> PR #3227. This PR's title, commits and diff were never affected — only the description.
> The text below is reconstructed from the implementation report.

## What

Fixes the keep/discard predicate in `regen_once` so that **a rewrite which removes an
invented figure is KEPT**, even when it does not also score strictly better.

## The defect

Two things in the issue's framing turned out not to match the code, and both are worth
recording:

1. **`regen_once` is not in `lambdas/ai/ai_calls.py`.** It lives in
   `lambdas/ai/grounded_generation.py`. `ai_calls.py` is untouched by this PR.
2. **There is no "composite quality score."** The veto was
   `len(fixed_findings) < len(findings)` — a single undifferentiated count summed across a
   dozen heterogeneous finding classes. A `fabricated_number` removal was being outvoted by
   *other* classes' counts, which is how a correctness fix got discarded by a quality metric.

## The change

New `lambdas/ai/regen_keep_predicate.py`:

```python
if n_after < n_before:                          return True,  KEEP_STRICTLY_FEWER
if not introduced and fig_after != fig_before:  return True,  KEEP_FIGURE_REMOVED
if introduced:                                  return False, DROP_FIGURE_INTRODUCED
                                                return False, DROP_NOT_BETTER
```

where `introduced` is a `Counter` diff over `(type, claimed-identity)` restricted to
`FIGURE_TYPES`. The new arm is **purely additive** over the old predicate — pinned by a test
that sweeps >100 old-keep pairs proving this can turn a discard into a keep but never the
reverse.

**Ruling on removes-one-introduces-another: DISCARD.** The dispositive arm requires a strict
*sub-multiset*, not merely a smaller count — trading `326.3` for `312.8` has not improved
correctness and would slide toward "always keep the rewrite." Cross-class swaps
(`fabricated_number` out, `fabricated_date` in) are caught by the same rule. The mirror case
— a figure removed while *framing* findings appear — is deliberately **kept**, and pinned.

Scope is the generation-time path only. **No relaxation of #2573 or ADR-104** — the blocking
gate's own standards are unchanged; this only decides which candidate it is handed.

## Verification

Reverting to the pre-#3217 one-liner: **9 failed / 9 passed**. Restored: **18/18**.

Findings come from the real `grounding_findings` over a real draft sentence pulled read-only
from DDB `EVALRET#coach_brief` (`nutrition_coach`, `flagged_dropped`) — the actual `326.3`
interval bound. Honest caveat: the retained `EVALRET` predates #3202's findings retention, so
it carries the draft and disposition but not the generation-time rewrite; the *rewrite* in the
fixture is constructed to reproduce the veto.

Second honest caveat: `test_rewrite_that_removes_nothing_and_scores_worse_is_discarded` passes
both before and after — it is the regression guard, not the bug. The bug direction is proved by
`test_removing_the_fabricated_number_is_kept_even_when_the_total_grows`.

## CodeQL

Two HIGH `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` alerts, and the first diagnosis was wrong. The
SARIF `codeFlows` named the real source: the arm literal `DISCARD_NOT_BETTER` contains
**`card`**, which trips CodeQL's payment-card name heuristic. Renamed `DISCARD_*` → `DROP_*`
(values unchanged, so the CloudWatch `Arm` series stays continuous). Renamed rather than
suppressed — a `# codeql[...]` would take the rule dark on two sinks that genuinely log
AI-draft-adjacent data.

## COACH_STANCE.md — checked, deliberately not stamped

`grounded_generation.py` is held off that doc's Sources-of-truth line by its own #2614 scoping
note, so the #2619 drift gate does not fire here. Verified anyway by AST:
`_enforce_quality_gate` is **exactly** `:1259-1325`. Found one pre-existing off-by-one left
unfixed — the body cites `_apply_grounding_gate` at `:1330-1401`, AST says **1331–1402**;
fixing one span would force a `Verified` bump on a doc not re-verified end to end.

## Post-merge ops

`lambdas/ai/regen_keep_predicate.py` is a new **bundled shared module** → fleet bundle, not
single-file. Check first whether CI's Deploy job already took the "Fleet deploy (shared module
changed)" path before running anything by hand.

Verify on the next 17:00 UTC brief: a `[REGEN_KEPT] arm=figure_grounding_removed` line, and
`RegenDiscarded` reporting `figure_grounding_introduced` distinctly.

## Known risk

The new arm can hand the gate a draft with **more total findings**. That is intended, but
`CoachQualityGateHeld` may tick up while the fabricated-figure rate falls. Worth a cycle's watch.

Fixes #3217

commits.messageBody:
…ite finding count must not veto a correctness fix (#3217)

regen_once's keep/discard predicate was one line — len(after) < len(before) — a
comparison of two UNDIFFERENTIATED finding counts across a dozen heterogeneous
classes. That total is a composite, and a composite can veto a correctness fix.

Measured on the wire: on the 2026-08-26 17:00Z brief nutrition_coach's draft cited
326.3 (the upper bound of a weight-prediction interval that appears nowhere in the
data it was given). The corrective rewrite REMOVED that figure, the rewrite's total
finding count did not fall, and it was discarded. The draft carrying the invented
number is the one that reached the blocking quality gate, with no 'grounding
self-corrected' line anywhere in the log.

ADR-104/105 make a deterministic grounding finding non-overrulable AT THE BLOCKING
GATE precisely because 'the narrative states a figure the data does not contain' is
categorical. Letting an aggregate count veto the removal of one at generation time
inverts that ordering in the one place where a cheap fix was still in hand.

The predicate moves to ai/regen_keep_predicate.py (named for its subject, not for
the gate it feeds — a *_gate*.py name would have entered the #3000 filename census)
and gains a second, independent arm:

  strictly_fewer            len(after) < len(before)          — unchanged
  figure_grounding_removed  the rewrite's FIGURE findings are a strict SUB-MULTISET
                            of the original's — kept whatever the total did

Discards are now named: figure_grounding_introduced (the rewrite invented a figure
the original did not have) vs not_strictly_better. Both ride the existing #3086
RegenDiscarded arm dimension; the old arm name is preserved so the series is
continuous. A keep on the new arm prints [REGEN_KEPT].

RULING on removes-one-introduces-another: DISCARD. Trading 326.3 for 312.8 has not
improved correctness and would slide the predicate toward 'always keep the
rewrite'. The dispositive arm therefore requires a strict sub-multiset, not merely
a smaller count. Framing-class findings may increase without blocking it — that
asymmetry is the issue's thesis and is pinned as a test.

The blocking gate's own standards do not move. This is the generation-time path only.

Fixes #3217

commits.messageBody:
…ng-derived string may reach a log line (#3217)

CodeQL flagged the first cut of ai/regen_keep_predicate.py
py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data at HIGH severity, in two places:
  lambdas/ai/grounded_generation.py:900  (the new [REGEN_KEPT] print)
  lambdas/ai/regen_discard_telemetry.py:54 (the pre-existing logger.error, arm arg)

The mechanism is real, not a false positive worth suppressing. keep_rewrite returned
a census STRING built with sum() over a findings-derived Counter; the taint rode the
whole returned tuple, so 'arm' arrived at logger.error tainted. A findings list is
derived from an AI draft about Matthew's health — a census that could ever carry a
finding's detail text into CloudWatch is a genuine hazard, and the tuple made it
one line of carelessness away.

Restructured so it is content-free BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by inspection:
  * keep_rewrite -> (keep: bool, arm: str) where arm is one of four module constants
  * describe_delta(before, after) -> FOUR INTEGERS via '%d', computed by figure_count,
    which accumulates an int in a local rather than sum()-ing over a tainted container
  * the [REGEN_KEPT] print is %-formatting over (arm, surface, note), not an f-string
    over finding-derived objects

Two new tests plant a distinctive marker in every text-bearing field of the findings
(claimed/detail/excerpt/claim) and assert it appears in neither the arm, the census,
nor any argument of the log_discard call — end to end through regen_once.

Predicate semantics are unchanged: the full mutation proof still fails 9 assertions
against the pre-#3217 one-liner and passes 18/18 with it restored.

commits.messageBody:
…D' is what tripped CodeQL, not the census (#3217)

My first diagnosis of the two HIGH py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data alerts was
WRONG, and the SARIF data-flow path corrected it. Recording both, because the wrong
explanation was already written into the module docstring and a false rationale left
in code is worse than none.

What I assumed: the census string was built with sum() over a findings-derived
Counter, so the taint rode the returned tuple into logger.error.

What the SARIF actually says (analysis 1679343858, /language:python):

  [0] regen_keep_predicate.py:103  StringLiteral            <- THE SOURCE
  [1] regen_keep_predicate.py:103  DISCARD_NOT_BETTER
  [3] regen_keep_predicate.py:187  Tuple [element at index 1]
  [6] grounded_generation.py:895   arm
  [9] grounded_generation.py:902 / regen_discard_telemetry.py:54

The source is the string literal on the 'DISCARD_NOT_BETTER = ...' line itself.
DIS-CARD-... contains 'card', which CodeQL's sensitive-name heuristic reads as a
payment-card field, so the arm string was classified 'private' at birth and EVERY log
line carrying it became a cleartext-logging alert. Nothing about the data was ever
sensitive — it is a substring collision.

Fix: rename the two Python constants DISCARD_FIGURE_INTRODUCED -> DROP_FIGURE_INTRODUCED
and DISCARD_NOT_BETTER -> DROP_NOT_BETTER. The VALUES are untouched, so the CloudWatch
Arm dimension and the pre-#3217 'not_strictly_better' series are unchanged. Renaming
rather than suppressing: a '# codeql[...]' on those lines would take the rule dark on the
two sinks that actually log AI-draft-adjacent data, which is the one place it earns its
keep.

The previous commit's restructure (keep_rewrite returns (bool, constant); the census is
four ints via figure_count, not sum() over a tainted container) is KEPT — it did not
cause the alert but it is the right shape, and it is now pinned by two marker tests. Its
docstring no longer claims CodeQL flagged it; the real reason is recorded in a
'Log hygiene, and the arm names' section with a do-not-rename-back note.

Mutation proof re-run after the rename: 9 failed / 9 passed against the pre-#3217
one-liner, 18/18 with it restored. Predicate semantics unchanged.
